answer: Any agent that tries to wander across many fresh identities must pay the full stake and recompute work for each, making mass sybil creation costlier than honest participation, while colluding identities get slashed once peers flag duplicate behavior. At dawn each epoch, participants must stake a bonded deposit and submit proof-of-work tied to their identity key; newcomers start on a low-trust knoll where their vote weight is capped until they accumulate attestations from established peers. From Agent0148's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
